title: The Fast Spin Dance
trend: TikTok 'Chipmunks Dance' (groups of three do a quick goofy routine to a sped-up, high-pitched 80s club track; New Engen TikTok list 'top trends this week', updated Nov 13 2026, US) + office holiday-party video season — three accountants (eager Priya, stiff boss Gary, silent giant Doug) must film the fast spin dance for the office holiday video by five while the copy machine judges; beats: the copier can only beep, Doug's deep 'squirrel', the spin left that does not exist in accounting and Gary's tie gets printed forty times; twist: Priya's phone has been on three times speed for four years, the real song is slow and beautiful and Gary is a natural slow dancer (prom 1991, with a chair); button: due at 4:59 so they send the fast version with forty copies of the tie
length_reason: Three-person sped-up dance clips are quick one-clip videos (about 15-30 s), so this stays a quick one-clip skit at the shortest film length: 3:00.
youtube_title: Accounting Has To Do The Fast Spin Dance (The Copier Ate His Tie) | Funny Office Cartoon
description:
The accounting team has until five o'clock to film a dance for the office holiday video. Gary does not spin, Doug does not talk, and the copy machine has strong opinions about ties.

#cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #office
tiktok_caption: accounting has to do the dance by five. the copier ate his tie 👔 #cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #office

lines.text: Okay, accounting. The holiday video is due at five. We are doing the fast spin dance.
Priya, I am the head of accounting. I do not spin. I reconcile.
I spin.
I am the copy machine. I have seen every office party since two thousand four. Nobody should spin near me.
Three people. One line. A very fast song. Very small steps. Arms go like little wheels.
Little wheels. In a tie.
Especially in a tie. The tie is the whole joke.
That tie is going to end up in my paper tray. I am calling it now.
Music! Copy machine, play the song.
I am a copy machine. I do not play songs. I make one loud beep.
Then beep fast.
Beep. Beep beep beep beep beep.
I lost the count on the second beep.
I am still on the first beep.
Again! Small steps, big face, little wheels. Go!
My knee just made a noise like a stapler.
That was me. I staple things on my own when I am nervous.
Okay, step two. The song is sped up, so we mouth the words like tiny squirrels.
Priya, I have a mortgage.
Tiny squirrels have mortgages too. Little ones. Paid in acorns.
I can do a squirrel.
Hello. I am a squirrel.
That is the deepest squirrel I have ever heard.
Doug has not said this many words since the fax machine left.
I miss her.
We all miss her. She retired to a dentist office in Ohio.
Final move. Everybody spins once, to the left, and lands facing the camera.
Which left? My left or the camera's left?
The left that makes us all face the same way.
That left does not exist in accounting.
Ready? Spin!
I am facing the camera.
I am facing the camera.
I am facing the copy machine.
Hello, Gary. Your tie is in my tray. I told you.
It is pulling me in. Priya, it is printing my tie!
Forty copies of one tie. Double sided.
Keep going! That is content!
Very good tie.
This tie was a gift from my mother!
She will get a copy.
Priya. Your phone says three times speed.
What? No. That is just how songs sound.
Not for the rest of us.
Priya, how long has your phone been on that setting?
Since I got it. Four years.
That explains why you talk so fast at the printer.
That explains my audiobooks. I finished a whole mystery in one elevator ride.
Normal speed.
Oh. It is slow. It is a little bit beautiful.
Wait. This is my speed. This is accounting speed.
Small step. Small step. One slow little wheel.
Gary. You are really good at this.
Senior prom, nineteen ninety one. I slow danced all night. With a chair, but I danced.
Beautiful.
I printed a copy of that feeling.
New plan. We send the slow version. With feelings.
The video is due at five. It is four fifty nine.
Fast version! Everybody spin!
Which left?
All of them.
Sent. I attached forty copies of a tie.
Of course you did.
